title: Retrospective: Data Mining Static Code Attributes to Learn Defect Predictors

edges.target: PROMISE repository (NASA defect data: CM1, JM1, KC1, PC1, ...)
edges.evidence: we built mutators that injected an increasing amount of their quality issues into PROMISE defect data sets. Strangely, the performance curve remained flat
edges.section: 5.2 Stranger Things (Menzies's 6th Law); footnote 8 lists CM1, JM1, KC1...PC5

edges.target: Shepperd et al. NASA data quality issues (repeated rows, illegal attributes)
edges.ref: [89] M. Shepperd, Q. Song, Z. Sun, C. Mair, Data quality: Some comments on the nasa software defect datasets, TSE 39(9), 2013
edges.evidence: Shepperd et al. [89] found numerous quality issues with PROMISE data... we built mutators that injected an increasing amount of their quality issues into PROMISE defect data sets

edges.target: Cohen 'straw man' benchmarking guidance (Empirical Methods for AI)
edges.ref: [94] P. R. Cohen, Empirical methods for artificial intelligence. MIT press, 1995
edges.evidence: Cohen argues that supposedly sophisticated methods should be benchmarked against seemingly stupider ones... whenever I checked a supposedly sophisticated method against a simpler one

edges.target: Hou et al. SLR of LLMs for SE (229 papers)
edges.ref: [81] X. Hou et al., Large language models for software engineering: A systematic literature review, TOSEM 33(8), 2024
edges.evidence: in a recent systematic review [81] of 229 SE papers using large language models (LLMs), only 13/229 = 5% of those papers compared LLMs to other approaches. This is a methodological error

edges.target: Grinsztajn et al. tree models beat deep learning on tabular data
edges.ref: [82] L. Grinsztajn, E. Oyallon, G. Varoquaux, Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on typical tabular data? NeurIPS'22
edges.evidence: other methods (developed and certified using PROMISE-style research) can produce results that are better and/or faster [82]-[88]

edges.target: Herbold et al. problems with SZZ / defect data collection
edges.ref: [53] S. Herbold, A. Trautsch, F. Trautsch, B. Ledel, Problems with szz and features..., EMSE 27(2), 2022
edges.evidence: little curation, little validation, often purely heuristic data collection without quality checks... all this newer data might not necessarily be better [52], [53]

edges.target: Menzies, Greenwald & Frank 2007 defect-prediction protocol and shared scripts/data
edges.ref: [1] T. Menzies, J. Greenwald, A. Frank, Data mining static code attributes to learn defect predictors, TSE 33(1), pp. 2-13, 2007
edges.evidence: It defined a set of steps to build and report the results of data mining... the paper shared all its scripts and data

not_reuse_examples: [32] Arcuri & Briand statistical guide: cited only inside a list about 'proactively fixing defects' [30]-[32]; no statistical test is applied in this paper.
[46]-[49] COC81, DESHARNIS, JM1, XALAN origin papers: named as over-used datasets the author now desk-rejects; not analysed here.
[51] CommitGuru and [50] Xia et al. 1100+ Github projects: pointed to as newer data sources readers could use; not executed or mined here.
[90] Nair et al. bad learners, [67] Turhan et al. transfer learning: prior results summarised as 'strange things' / laws, background only.
notes: Retrospective/position paper (arXiv 2501.15662) on the 2007 TSE paper and the PROMISE repository; no new experiments except a one-paragraph mention of a mutator study on PROMISE defect data, so reuse edges are few and mostly sanitycheck/methodology; no steppingstone, statmethod or software edges.
